name: Horns
description: Soft brass for swells and distant lines: horn, flugelhorn, trumpet open or muted and low brass, brighter as they get louder, with a section of players on every key.

params.name: Type
params.description: Which instrument plays. Each has its own bell, from the round dark horn to the thin nasal muted trumpet, and its own way of speaking.

params.name: Blow
params.description: How hard the players blow. Low is a pure warm hum; high is a bright blare. The tone brightens as each note swells and darkens as it fades.

params.name: Breath
params.description: Air in the tone: breath noise that rings through the tube at the pitch of the note. High with a gentle Blow, the note is half air.

params.name: Section
params.description: From one player to four on every key, further apart in tuning, timing and place as it rises. At zero a single steady player sits in the centre.

params.name: Attack
params.description: How long a note takes to arrive, from a tongued start to a slow swell. Low notes always speak a little later than high ones.

params.name: Release
params.description: How long a note takes to recede after the key is released. The brightness leaves before the body of the tone does.

params.name: Vibrato
params.description: Depth of a slow waver in pitch that waits a moment and then eases in, as a player adds it to a held note.

params.name: Harmony
params.description: Adds a second voice that follows every note in parallel: a fourth below to the left of centre, a fifth above to the right. At centre it is silent.

params.name: Volume
params.description: Output level of the instrument. A soft clip after it rounds off the peaks when many notes stack up.

origin.note: Written for live-mix on cpp/kit. Models soft orchestral and jazz brass (French horn, flugelhorn, trumpet open and with a Harmon-style mute, trombone and tuba as low brass) as an open-loop driven pipe: a breath envelope drives a closed-form harmonic series whose brightness rises with the pressure (the brass rule Risset found in trumpet tones, the small-amplitude power law of Worman and Benade), lagging on the way up, through a bell filter fixed in hertz. Grounded in the project's acoustic research notes (Risset and Mathews, Beauchamp, Meyer, Fletcher and Rossing, Hirschberg). Simplified: no lip valve or bore waveguide, so no register breaks or cracked notes; one shared bell per type instead of one per note; each note is levelled so loudness follows the envelope while colour follows the pressure; the harmony voice is a second oscillator, not a pitch shifter, so its formant does not move and it has no splice artefacts. Choices rather than measurements of an original: the bell formants (French horn 340 Hz, trumpet 1300 Hz and low brass 480 Hz follow figures recalled from Meyer; flugelhorn 800 Hz is a guess between them), the whole muted voicing (two high-passes, the second with a resonant corner near 1.8 kHz), the brightness range of each type, the lag, lip settle, scatter and vibrato figures. Not a circuit or sample emulation.
